$comment: Architectural boundary rules enforced by scripts/check-arch.sh. Typed match_argv checks declare match and no-match exit codes; filters are ordered Python regular expressions over matched output lines.

rules.description: Credentials must never enter version control.
rules.what: A hardcoded credential appears in a tracked file.
rules.why: Anything committed stays in git history permanently, even if a later commit deletes it.
rules.fix: Move the value into .env (gitignored) or the OS keychain, read it through an env var, then rotate the exposed credential — it must be treated as compromised.

rules.what: The .env file is tracked by git.
rules.why: That is where real credentials live; tracking it publishes them to every clone and fork.
rules.fix: Run: git rm --cached .env && echo .env >> .gitignore — then rotate every credential it contained.

rules.description: Debug statements must not survive into committed source.
rules.what: A debugger or debug-print statement remains in source.
rules.why: Debug artifacts change runtime behaviour and are a reliable signal that a session ended without cleanup.
rules.fix: Delete the statement. If the output is genuinely needed, route it through the project logger instead.

rules.description: Conflict markers must never be committed.
rules.what: An unresolved merge conflict marker is present in a tracked file.
rules.why: The file is syntactically broken; whatever verification passed did not actually cover this path.
rules.fix: Open the named file, resolve the conflict by hand, then re-run the full verification command.
